citation: Abramowitz, M. and Stegun, I. A., eds. (1964), Handbook of Mathematical Functions, National Bureau of Standards Applied Mathematics Series 55 -- Table 26.1, 'Normal Probability Function and Derivatives', p. 966, column P(x), tabulated to 15 decimal places.
notes: P(x) is the standard normal distribution function, defined at the foot of the table page as the integral of Z(t) from minus infinity to x. Four rows are transcribed at x = 1.00, 1.50, 2.00 and 2.50. WHAT THIS CASE CLAIMS: fifteen published decimal places survive the mapping branch of to_mcp without narrowing or rounding, which the 'exact' class states by refusing a difference of one representable step. It claims nothing about any method; no code here computes P(x).
